claim: MERFISH allows genome-scale imaging of RNAs in individual cells in intact tissues.
source: Multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) allows genome-scale imaging of RNAs in individual cells in intact tissues.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known capability of MERFISH.

claim: MERFISH has been applied to image thin-tissue samples of ~10 µm thickness to date.
source: To date, MERFISH has been applied to image thin-tissue samples of ~10 µm thickness.

claim: The thick-tissue 3D MERFISH imaging method uses confocal microscopy for optical sectioning.
source: Here, we present a thick-tissue three-dimensional (3D) MERFISH imaging method, which uses confocal microscopy for optical sectioning, deep learning for increasing imaging speed and quality, as well as sample preparation and imaging protocol optimized for thick samples.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a component of the method.

claim: The thick-tissue 3D MERFISH imaging method uses deep learning for increasing imaging speed and quality.

evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a component of the method.

claim: 3D MERFISH was demonstrated on mouse brain tissue sections of up to 200 µm thickness with high detection efficiency and accuracy.
source: We demonstrated 3D MERFISH on mouse brain tissue sections of up to 200 µm thickness with high detection efficiency and accuracy.

claim: Spatial genomics enables in situ gene-expression profiling of complex tissues with high spatial resolution.

evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Spatial genomics allows for the identification and spatial mapping of molecularly defined cell types in intact tissues.
source: Spatial genomics enables in situ gene-expression profiling of complex tissues with high spatial resolution, allowing for the identification and spatial mapping of molecularly defined cell types in intact tissues (Bressan et al., 2023; Larsson et al., 2021; Zhuang, 2021; Close et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The spinning-disk confocal detection geometry cuts a large amount of in-focus fluorescence signals.

claim: MERFISH imaging was performed to measure 242 genes in tissue sections of the mouse cerebral cortex.

claim: A neural network was trained based on a subset of short- and long-exposure-time image pairs and used to improve the quality of the remaining images taken with short exposure time.

claim: Deep learning improved the SNR of the 0.1 s images substantially.

source: Third, we aligned the images taken during each imaging round based on the fiducial bead images, accounting for x-y drift in the stage position relative to the first round of imaging.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A high-pass filter was applied to the enhanced images for each FOV to remove cellular background.
source: Fourth, a high-pass filter was then applied to the enhanced images for each FOV to remove cellular background.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The filtered images were deconvolved using 20 rounds of Lucy–Richardson deconvolution to tighten RNA spots.
source: The filtered images were then deconvolved using 20 rounds of Lucy–Richardson deconvolution to tighten RNA spots and low-pass filtered to account for small movements in the apparent centroid of RNAs between imaging rounds.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Individual RNA molecules were identified by pixel-based decoding algorithm.
source: Individual RNA molecules were identified by pixel-based decoding algorithm as described previously (Fang et al., 2022; Xia et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with supporting citations.

claim: Barcodes were independently assigned to each pixel, then aggregated adjacent pixels with the same barcodes into putative RNA molecules.
source: Briefly, we independently assigned barcodes to each pixel, then aggregated adjacent pixels with the same barcodes into putative RNA molecules and filtered the list of putative RNA molecules to enrich for correctly identified transcripts (Xia et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: The intensity of each image in a bit was normalized by median intensity across all FOVs in the bit to eliminate the intensity variation between hybridization rounds and color channels.
source: To aid comparison, we normalized intensity of each image in a bit by median intensity across all FOVs in the bit to eliminate the intensity variation between hybridization rounds and color channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Pixels with the Euclidean distance larger than 0.65 away from any valid barcode were excluded.
source: We excluded pixels with the Euclidean distance larger than 0.65 away from any valid barcode in the first step and disregarded any pixels with an intensity less than 10 as they were potentially due to off-target binding probes as observed previously (Moffitt et al., 2016b) or noise-induced artifacts amplified by the deep learning algorithm.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: The list of putative RNA molecules was filtered to enrich for correctly identified transcripts for an overall barcode misidentification rate at 5%.
source: After assigning barcodes to each pixel independently, we aggregated adjacent pixels that were assigned with the same barcodes into putative RNA molecules, and then filtered the list of putative RNA molecules to enrich for correctly identified transcripts for an overall barcode misidentification rate at 5%, as described previously (Xia et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: Putative RNAs that contained only a single pixel were removed as they likely arose from background of spurious barcodes.
source: We further removed putative RNAs that contained only a single pixel as they likely arose from background of spurious barcodes generated by random fluorescent fluctuations and had a higher misidentification rate than those that contained two or more pixels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Redundant molecules present in adjacent z-intervals were removed to avoid counting duplicate molecules.
source: Finally, since we imaged samples at 1 µm z-intervals, it is possible to capture the same molecule in multiple z-intervals. To avoid counting duplicate molecules, we remove the redundant molecules present in adjacent z-intervals prior to assigning barcodes to individual cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Cell segmentation was performed on the co-staining of DAPI and total polyA mRNA using the deep learning-based cell segmentation algorithm, Cellpose 2.0.
source: We performed cell segmentation on the co-staining of DAPI and total polyA mRNA using the deep learning-based cell segmentation algorithm, Cellpose 2.0 (Pachitariu and Stringer, 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: The segmentation model was fine-tuned with the user-in-the-loop approach of the Cellpose 2.0 using randomly selected z-slices.
source: We fine-tuned the segmentation model with the user-in-the-loop approach of the Cellpose 2.0 using randomly selected z-slices containing the DAPI and polyA mRNA channels with the 'CP' model as a starting point.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The segmentation model was applied to 3D z-stacks for each FOV to generate segmentation mask in 3D using Cellpose 2.0 using its 3D mode.
source: After human-guided training, we applied the segmentation model to 3D z-stacks for each FOV to generate segmentation mask in 3D using Cellpose 2.0 using its 3D mode.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Duplicated cells that appeared in adjacent FOVs were identified and removed based on overlapping volume.
source: Owing to an approximate 10% overlap between adjacent FOVs, it is possible that a single cell may be captured in two adjacent FOVs, resulting in duplicated cells. To address this issue, we used the following procedure to remove overlapping cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Two cells were considered duplicates if their overlapping ratio was larger than 40%, and the cell of smaller volume was removed.
source: We considered two cells duplicates if their overlapping ratio was larger than 40% and, in this case, the cell of smaller volume was removed.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Cells with a small volume (<100 μm2), or low RNA count number (<30), or those captured in fewer than 5 or more than 40 adjacent 1 μm z-sections were excluded.
source: Specifically, we excluded cells with a small volume (<100 μm2), or low RNA count number (<30), or those captured in fewer than 5 or more than 40 adjacent 1 μm z-sections.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: ~10% cells were removed as putative doublets identified using doubletFinder.
source: Next, we removed ~10% cells as putative doublets identified using doubletFinder (McGinnis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: The single-cell data was analyzed using Seurat.
source: After the above preprocessing steps, we then analyzed the single-cell data using Seurat (Stuart et al., 2019) as described below.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: The gene vector for each cell was normalized by dividing each cell by its total RNA counts sum and then multiplying the resulting number with a constant number 10,000.
source: We normalized the gene vector for each cell by dividing each cell by its total RNA counts sum and then multiply the resulting number with a constant number 10,000 to ensure all cells contain the same total RNA counts.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A log transformation was performed on the cell-by-gene matrix after normalization.
source: Following this normalization, we performed a log transformation on the cell-by-gene matrix.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The normalized single-cell expression profiles were z-scored, followed by dimensionality reduction by principal component analysis.
source: The normalized single-cell expression profiles were z-scored, followed by dimensionality reduction by principal component analysis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The first 30 principal components were used to perform graph-based Louvain community detection.
source: We then used the first 30 principal components and performed graph-based Louvain community detection (Blondel et al., 2008) in the 30 principal components space with nearest-neighborhood size k = 15 and resolution r = 0.8 (default in Seurat) to identify clusters.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section with a supporting citation.

claim: Excitatory neuronal, inhibitory neuronal, and non-neuronal cell types were identified based on the expression of the canonical marker genes from the first round of clustering.
source: From the first round of clustering, we identified excitatory neuronal, inhibitory neuronal, and non-neuronal cell types based on the expression of the canonical marker genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The procedure of dimensionality reduction and clustering was repeated for the excitatory and inhibitory neurons separately to further refine cell classification.
source: To further refine our cell classification, we then repeated the procedure of dimensionality reduction and clustering, as described above, for the excitatory and inhibitory neurons separately.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: For the identification of neuronal clusters, the parameters k = 15 and r = 5 were used for inhibitory neurons and k = 15 and r = 3 for excitatory neurons.
source: For the identification of neuronal clusters, we used the following parameters k = 15 and r = 5 for inhibitory neurons and k = 15 and r = 3 for excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: For the mouse cortex 3D MERFISH data, subcortical areas were excluded.
source: For the mouse cortex 3D MERFISH data, we excluded the subcortical areas.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: L6b cells were used as a landmark to guide the exclusion of subcortical areas in the data.
source: Specifically, we used L6b cells, which form a thin layer that separates white matter from gray matter, as a landmark to guide the exclusion of subcortical areas in our data.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Cells from L2/3 to L6b were kept in the analysis.
source: In our analysis, we kept cells from L2/3 to L6b.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: For each interneuron, its nearest-neighboring neurons were identified in the 3D MERFISH images.
source: To perform this analysis, for each interneuron, we first identified its nearest-neighboring neurons in the 3D MERFISH images.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Nearest-neighbor pairs were classified into 'to-self' (same subtype) and 'to-other' (different subtypes) groups.
source: We further classified these nearest-neighbor pairs into two groups: 'to-self' (same subtype) and 'to-other' (different subtypes) based on whether the neighboring pairs belong to the same subtypes of interneurons ('to-self') or an interneuron and a neuron of different type or subtype (excitatory or inhibitory) ('to-other').
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The Euclidean distance in 3D was calculated for the nearest-neighbor pairs.
source: We then calculated their Euclidean distance in 3D.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.

claim: For each interneuron, the nearest-neighbor interneuron (regardless of which subtypes of interneurons it belongs to) was identified and their Euclidean distance in 3D space was calculated.
source: To obtain the nearest-neighbor distance distribution for interneurons shown in Figure 3f and h, for each interneuron, we identified the nearest-neighbor interneuron (regardless of which subtypes of interneurons it belongs to) and then calculated their Euclidean distance in 3D space.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Materials and methods section.
